newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's names chairman of U.S. business.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's names chairman of U.S. business.

text.p: McDonald's Corp. said Tuesday it created a new position of chairman of its U.S. operations as part of a management realignment.
McDonald's said the new position will be filled by Jack Greenberg, currently vice chairman and chief financial officer.
Greenberg will relinquish the chief financial officer post, but remains vice chairman of the company. He will continue to report to Michael Quinlan, McDonald's chairman.
Edward Rensi, McDonald's U.S.A. president and chief executive officer, will report directly to Greenberg, the fast-food giant said.
McDonald's also said it named Michael Conley, currently senior vice president and controller, as chief financial officer, succeeding Greenberg.
The company, which operates 19,200 restaurants in 94 countries, said the changes were aimed at strengthening its U.S. management.
"While these changes are evolutionary, they will bring more management firepower where we need it, both for the short and long-term," Quinlan said in a statement.

"In a complex, dynamic and difficult U.S. marketplace, we are focusing on delivering great food taste, enhancing the quality of service, strengthening strategic marketing and adding new restaurants," Quinlan added.
In the international arena, which produces more than half of McDonald's operating income, Quinlan said the company is just beginning to tap what he called "enormous markets."
As chairman of McDonald's U.S.A., Greenberg will work with Rensi and his team, as well as U.S. franchisees, to provide strategic direction in the U.S. market, the company said.
In other management moves, Christopher Pieszko, vice president and U.S. controller, was named vice president and corporate controller, reporting to Conley.

Paul Schrage, senior executive vice president, chief marketing officer and a board member, has announced his intention to retire within a year. He will continue as chairman of Ronald McDonald House Charities.
McDonald's said it also changed responsibilities of two senior marketing executives.

David Green, senior vice president, marketing, will fill a newly created position as the senior marketing officer of McDonald's International. He will report directly to James Cantalupo, president and chief executive officer of McDonald's International.
Brad Ball, senior vice president of U.S.A. marketing, takes over full responsibility for U.S. Marketing, and will report directly to Rensi.
